subject: Packaging fit & tier-flex proposal for AcmeCloud pilot
messages:
From: Alex Hudson <alex.hudson@acmecloud.com>
To: rafael_mendes@redwood.com
Cc: procure@acmecloud.com
Date: Mon, 05 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Packaging options and pilot scope for AcmeCloud

Hi Rafael,

Thanks for the demo last week — the latency numbers looked solid. Our technical team asked me to get clarity on packaging: they want to understand the upgrade/downgrade mechanics, what features are bundled in each tier, and how discounts apply during pilot -> production transition.

Quick background: we'll be piloting a document ingestion + search feature with ~100k monthly queries, spiky daytime traffic, and a hard 300ms P95 latency target. We care about predictable unit cost and the ability to step up capacity quickly if we hit production needs.

Could you share a short summary of: 1) which tier you'd recommend for the pilot vs production, 2) how feature bundling (observability / prefix caching / priority routing) maps to tiers, and 3) discounting approach for a 12–18 month commitment if we move to Dedicated? Attached is our internal pilot acceptance plan (AcmeCloud-MAP-v2.pdf).

Appreciate it — Alex

--
Alex Hudson
Director, Platform Engineering | AcmeCloud
From: rafael_mendes@redwood.com
To: Alex Hudson <alex.hudson@acmecloud.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 05 Jul 2026 12:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Packaging options and pilot scope for AcmeCloud

Alex — thanks for the MAP and context. Short answer up top: start pilot on Compact (hosted) with observability add-on + KV prefix caching; for production, Dedicated capacity with a two-step runway (Committed baseline + burst pool). Below is a concise mapping and next steps.

Summary recommendations
- Pilot (Compact hosted):
  - Why: fastest time-to-value, minimal onboarding. Covers 100k/mo with headroom via burst credits.
  - Included features: standard logging, basic console dashboards. Add-on: Observability Pro (+token-level cost breakdown) and Prefix KV cache.
  - Upgrade path: zero-downtime roll to Dedicated — we can pin model versions and retain KV cache via snapshotting.

- Production (Dedicated):
  - Why: predictable throughput, regional isolation, SLA options.
  - Bundle: Dedicated (baseline GPUs) + Priority Routing + Extended Retention for traces.
  - Burst pool: pay-as-you-go bursts for sudden traffic spikes.

Discounting and term guidance
- 12-month commit: standard tiered discount (10% off hosted list, or equivalent committed spend credit for Dedicated).
- 18-month commit: additional incentive (up to 18% effective discount) tied to reserved baseline capacity and a short onboarding credit applied during first 3 months.
- We can structure an early-conversion credit during pilot: if you convert to Dedicated within 60 days of pilot completion, we credit back 50% of pilot spend against baseline for the first billing cycle.

Feature bundling details (how they map to SKUs)
- Observability Pro: token-level cost + 90-day retention (bundled on Dedicated; add-on for hosted).
- Prefix/KV cache: deployed on runtime level; recommended for chat/document workloads to reduce token cost.
- Priority routing: required for regional failover + SLA-backed latency targets.

Operational notes
- Upgrade/downgrade mechanics: upgrades are immediate (route-based cutover). Downgrades require a 14-day notice to schedule capacity reallocation and potential cache warm-up.
- Rollout strategy: canary traffic first 10% -> 50% -> 100% with automatic fallback to hosted during degraded performance.

Next steps
1) Share expected peak qps and 95/99 latency targets (you gave 300ms P95 — we also need P99 target).
2) I'll loop Ben (dedicated capacity lead) and Kim (finance/discounts) to draft a 1-page commercial for your procurement team.
3) If you want, we can run a short cost-sensitivity model — I request your expected token mix (generation vs embeddings) for that.

I'll attach a pricing matrix and a sample pilot SOW in the follow-up.

Thanks,

--
Rafael Mendes
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: rafael_mendes@redwood.com
To: ben_carter@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 05 Jul 2026 12:04:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Packaging options and pilot scope for AcmeCloud

FW: AcmeCloud MAP attached. They want clear guidance on pilot->Dedicated conversion credits and an 18-month discount structure tied to reserved baseline capacity.

Key asks I want us to answer in the one-pager:
- Proposed baseline GPU count for a Dedicated pilot if they choose to pilot on Dedicated instead of hosted (we should still recommend hosted Compact first but include dedicated pilot numbers).
- Discount ladder for 12 vs 18 months (include effective % and any onboarding credits).
- Downgrade mechanics: explicit timelines and any data retention caveats.

Ben — can you run a quick capacity estimate for 100k qps/month with 300ms P95 and spiky traffic (we need baseline + burst)? Kim — what's the most aggressive commercial we can offer for an 18-month baseline while protecting margin?

Thanks — Rafael
From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: rafael_mendes@redwood.com
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 06 Jul 2026 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Packaging options and pilot scope for AcmeCloud

Rafael — quick calc attached as redwood-pricing-matrix.xlsx (high level). Baseline recommendation if they want Dedicated pilot: 2x A100-equivalent nodes with autoscale to 4 nodes as burst. That should cover 100k queries/month with headroom for spikes; P95 ~220–300ms depending on sequence lengths.

If they start on hosted Compact and convert, our snapshot + routing approach keeps KV cache warmup to a couple hours for most doc workloads — not zero, but acceptable. For discounts:
- 12mo: 12% off list for baseline reserved commit (minimum commit $75k/mo).
- 18mo: 18% off list + first-90-day onboarding credit equal to 25% of their pilot billed usage (capped).

I'll hand the commercial outline to Kim for ironing — these numbers assume typical generation/embedding split you described.

-ben

--
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: kimberly_park@redwood.com
To: rafael_mendes@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 07 Jul 2026 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Packaging options and pilot scope for AcmeCloud

Team — agree with Ben's capacity sketch. Commercial guidance: we can offer the 18% effective discount on committed baseline if AcmeCloud signs a 18-month MSLA and agrees to a 6-week onboarding SOW (discount contingent on signing the SOW). The onboarding credit language should be: "Pilot credit applied against first billing cycle of baseline upon conversion, capped at the lesser of pilot spend or $50k."

On downgrade language: require 30 days' notice for baseline reduction >30%; retention and audit logs beyond 90 days are billable as an add-on to avoid large storage delta.

I'll draft the one-pager and attach redwood-pricing-matrix.xlsx + SOW template. Rafael — once you get Acme's P99 target and token mix, we'll finalize numbers for procurement.

Kim

--
Kimberly Park
Director, Revenue Operations | Redwood Inference
